sentence: This project tests whether electronic health records can help find patients likely to have rare genetic diseases, so diagnosis takes less time.
This project produces pigs with edited genes to supply lung, kidney and heart organs for transplantation.
This project studies how the brain combines cues from different senses to guide social interactions between animals, using a rove beetle.
This project collects cancer case records and links them to healthcare claims data so researchers can study cancer in real-world populations.
This project builds a magnetic resonance imaging technology that lets children with electronic implants be imaged safely.
This project builds a deep neural network imaging tool that judges whether breast tissue is still alive right after focused ultrasound ablation.
This project develops implantable microdevices that release tiny doses of many drugs inside a patient's tumor and show how the tumor responds to each.
This project studies how social settings and social stress relate to loss of control over eating in Black adolescents with overweight or obesity.
This project provides research tools and support to improve the prevention and treatment of human digestive diseases.
This project builds cytokine support that acts only in tumors to help engineered T cell therapy work better against pancreatic cancer.
This project studies whether early primary care follow-up after discharge helps patients with pneumonia and hypoxemia avoid returning to the hospital.
This project studies how cholesterol harms the liver in alcohol-associated hepatitis and tests a way to restore cholesterol balance in liver cells.
This project studies how G proteins that are switched on by mutations are controlled inside cells.
This project studies the cells and processes that drive post-traumatic osteoarthritis, a joint disease that follows injury.
This project studies how low oxygen in the brain, seen with diffuse optical tomography, links delirium to later cognitive decline.
This project supports research teams with management and statistical analysis in work on pediatric cancers driven by fusion oncoproteins.
This project studies the daily stress and reactions of caregivers for older adults with Lewy Body Dementia.
This project studies regulatory proteins that guide normal craniofacial development to find out what causes the rare disease Schneckenbecken dysplasia.
This project builds a visualization tool that adds ultrasound to laparoscopy so surgeons can see hidden tumors and blood vessels below organ surfaces.
This project studies what satellite DNA, a type of repeated sequence in genomes, does and how it evolves.
